question.problem:
The matrix $D$ is given below. Let ${d}_{1}$, ${d}_{2}$, and ${d}_{3}$ be the respective columns of $D.$ Determine if $B=\text{{}{d}_{1},{d}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(D).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${d}_{2}={x}_{1}{d}_{1}+{x}_{3}{d}_{3}.$ 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ -4 & 24 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

current_example.problem:
The matrix $A$ is given below. Let $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a}_2$, and $\mathbf{a}_3$ be the respective columns of $A.$ Determine if ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128538/assets/80ca26ec81af01cb4ae66568ce515953859293a9b6d326098f46cce86cb88e80.svg) is a basis of $\textrm{Col}(A).$ 
If that is the case, find $x_1 \cdot x_2$, where $\mathbf{a}_3=x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128538/assets/dc2d69a54916038f80bf1dc03c5c61200c5b86915ee22ed6602f82aec32be502.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $A$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 9 \\ 3 & 1 & 17\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 9 \\ 0 & -5 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-\frac{1}{5}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\textrm{Col}(A)$ is $\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2 \},$ that is to say,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128538/assets/b2ca81d364d29088b67fa7254626e1a6602d0ae69946e6e999070e6af1a57744.svg)

Now, since the $3$rd column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express $\mathbf{a}_3$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128538/assets/1dff88142aae5ab830fb63b433aada76b0961726f4439e1d92089d04bec3bbfc.svg)

This gives us $x_1 \cdot x_2 = 5 \cdot 2=10.$
